package.name: sidewalk_evaluation
package.description:
Phase 5 — quantitative evaluation of mapping and localization performance for the autonomous sidewalk robot.
This package turns recorded runs into numbers: absolute and relative trajectory error against a reference, drift per distance travelled, loop-closure and relocalization behaviour, processing latency and system load, and depth-sensor characterization against a flat wall at known distances. It then renders those numbers into plots and a single self-contained HTML report that can be emailed or opened offline.
The core research contribution of the project is a like-for-like comparison of three localization stacks — RTAB-Map (primary), the ZED SDK's own positional tracking, and ORB-SLAM3 — evaluated on identical recorded input. This package is the instrument that performs that comparison.
All maths is implemented directly on numpy so that the evaluation runs on a freshly flashed Jetson with no extra Python packages installed. The `evo` toolkit may optionally be used as an independent cross-check, but nothing here depends on it.
package.author: THAW ZIN
